stem:
The diagram shows six triangles meeting at centre $O$.

Which claim explains why these triangles form a regular hexagon?

options.text: Six congruent equilateral triangles fit around $O$ because six $60^{\circ}$ angles sum to $360^{\circ}$, so the outer boundary has equal sides and equal $120^{\circ}$ angles.
Call the answer regular hexagon, and stop with no angle sum at $O$.
Any six triangles around $O$ form a regular hexagon, even when the triangles are not congruent and not equilateral.
The same assembly also builds a regular pentagon from five such triangles around $O$.

teacher.key_rationale: Six 60° angles fill 360° at the centre; congruent equilateral triangles give equal outer sides and 120° hexagon angles. Naming regular hexagon alone substitutes a label. Dropping congruence/equilateral omits the needed conditions. Extending the rule to a pentagon is out of scope.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote inscribed-hexagon source as six equilateral triangles meeting at O with a marked 60° angle.
